decisions.title: Notification decision log
decisions.subtitle: What the engine decided and what the pipeline actually did, platform-wide: counts only, with no family or child identifier and no message text.
decisions.aggregateOnly: This is a platform-wide operations view. It shows no family, no child and no notification text — aggregate counts and type names only.
decisions.window: Window as the server resolved it
decisions.emptyHint: No notification decision was recorded in this window. This is not a zero.
decisions.sliceEmpty: No rows in this slice for the current window and filter.
decisions.remainderWhy: The server returned the top {{limit}} rows only and never counted the tail, so there is no number for it. A zero here would be an invention.
decisions.byAudienceHint: Parent vs child. One event may legitimately produce two independent decisions with two audiences.
decisions.bySourceHint: What set the decision off: a domain event, a periodic scan, a streak watch, a safety signal…
decisions.byProvenanceHint: Which decision provider produced the verdict. One today; the column exists so the question still has an answer when a second one ships.
decisions.byDateHint: The household's own day, not UTC — a decision at midnight in Cairo is filed under the family's next day.
decisions.byTypeHint: Top {{limit}} types only: the type vocabulary is open and grows with the product, so the list is deliberately bounded.
decisions.topCausesHint: The event that actually happened — not the message type. Top {{limit}} causes only.

provenance.actualHint: Measured from rows that exist in the database.

provenance.alwaysForecast: This metric is always a forecast: it multiplies a measured number by an assumed margin.

gap.referralAdminSummary: Admin referral figures (codes issued, sent, rewards, fraud rejections by reason) are exposed by no admin endpoint. `/referral/me` is a parent surface for one family; reading it here would be both wrong and a privacy regression.
gap.productAiMetrics: AI sessions, goals created and completed, and rewards redeemed are not in growth contract v1.0.
gap.cohortRetention: Retention is available per country as a snapshot; there is no cohort breakdown.
gap.refunds: Refunds are recorded in payment_transactions but the growth contract exposes no aggregate for them.
gap.activeChildren: There is no ACTIVE_CHILDREN KPI. `childrenAdded` is a daily flow, not a stock; using it as a stock drifts upward forever.
gap.activeParents: There is no parent-level activity signal. `dashboard-metrics` counts devices seen in the last 7 days and the families that own them — a device is not a person.
gap.familiesByCountry: Registered and active family counts exist platform-wide only, with no country split. `newRegistrations` is a daily flow, not a stock, and dividing the platform total between the two markets by any ratio available here would be a guess.
gap.subscriptionPlanMix: The database knows the plan tier and the billing period (monthly / annual), but no admin endpoint aggregates them. `activePaidSubscriptions` is a single number with no plan breakdown.
gap.pilotEnrollment: The pilot service writes invitations, cohorts and redemptions, but no controller exposes a read of them. Only the pilot's configuration is readable.
gap.safetyEvents: Safety incidents reach an operator today only as AI_SAFETY_INCIDENT alerts — one row per threshold breach, not a per-country count of events.

funnel.title: Funnel — impression to renewal
funnel.subtitle: Counts are families, not events: a family with three children crosses CHILD_ADDED once.
funnel.fromMeasurableTop: From the first step we measure (INSTALL)
funnel.monotonicityHint: A step outnumbering the one before it. Reported, never zeroed — usually an incomplete ad-platform import.
funnel.activationTitle: Activation — the metric the product lives or dies on
funnel.activationHint: A child — not a parent — completed a real goal and was actually rewarded. Families that reach this step stay.
funnel.timeToValueHint: Median gap between family creation and activation — median, not mean.

overview.title: Executive overview
overview.subtitle: Egypt and Saudi Arabia side by side, each in its own currency.
overview.currencyNote: Every money figure is shown in its own market's currency. There is no combined total, because that needs an exchange rate — a financial decision nobody has taken.
overview.noCombinedMoneyHint: Adding EGP to SAR without a declared rate is a lie. Pick a market to see its figures.

forecast.title: Quarterly forecast & targets
forecast.subtitle: Three fields per metric per quarter, and none of them is merged.
forecast.assumptionsHint: Assumptions are returned with every number derived from them, so you can disagree with the inputs rather than the output.
forecast.rateOutOfRange: A rate must be between 0 and 1.
forecast.modelNote: The model is a monthly roll-forward with constant leakage. It is not a survival model and will lean optimistic in the first quarter.

grants.title: Manual plan grants
grants.intro: Give a household full features without a payment — a tester, a pilot family, a support gesture — and take it back afterwards. Every grant ends on a date and is written to the audit log with your reason.
grants.emailHint: The household is resolved from this address on the server. There is no family id to type.
grants.reasonHint: Required. It is what makes this grant explainable months from now.
grants.revokeConfirm: This revokes EVERY entitlement on the household, including any from a real payment. Continue?
grants.liveNone: No live entitlement. The household is on the free tier.
grants.catalogueEmpty: The plan catalogue is empty, so this tier includes nothing. Nothing was granted.
grants.modeFeaturesHint: Comps the six keys you tick. Works on any database, including one whose plan catalogue is empty.
grants.modePlanHint: Comps whatever the tier currently includes, read from the plan catalogue — and follows the catalogue if it is edited later. Refuses if the catalogue is empty.
grants.catalogueEmptyAction: Define the tier in Plans & pricing first

accounts.title: Platform accounts
accounts.intro: Every household on the platform, one row each. This is the only view here that returns rows rather than totals — it is what "how many users and what state are they in" actually needs. No child name or date of birth is carried.

health.title: Platform health
health.intro: What the running container reports about itself: which build, which schema it is sitting on, and which dependency is or is not ready. Before this screen the only way to see any of it was to read deploy logs.
health.schemaNoLedger: This database has no Prisma migration ledger. `prisma migrate deploy` has never run against it.
health.schemaHalfMigrated: HALF-MIGRATED — a migration started and never finished, or was rolled back
health.schemaUnsupported: This build predates schema reporting. Redeploy to measure the applied migrations.

catalogue.title: Plan catalogue
catalogue.intro: What this platform sells. Every paid feature is decided from this table — nothing is pre-filled, because a price nobody chose is a price a customer eventually pays.
catalogue.emptyConsequence: The catalogue is EMPTY. While it is, every paid feature is locked for every household and a real purchase grants nothing — including whatever the FREE tier was meant to include.
catalogue.name: Name

household.title: Household detail
household.reasonHint: Required before any action here. It is what the audit row carries, and what makes the action explainable later.
household.suspendConfirm: Suspending blocks this person from signing in. It is reversible and removes nothing. Continue?

jobs.title: Scheduled jobs
jobs.intro: Every registered job, when it last ran, what it did, and what broke. These five endpoints have been behind the operator key since Phase C; until now the only way to answer «did the sweep run last night» was to read container logs.
jobs.name: Job
jobs.notRegistered: NO HANDLER — this row exists in the database and no code answers to it. It can never run.
jobs.alerting: Alerting — three or more consecutive failures
jobs.noFailures: No run failed in the window.
jobs.confirmRunBody: This bypasses the schedule and nothing else: the lease still applies, so it will not race a running replica, and the run key still applies, so work already done today is skipped rather than repeated. Some jobs delete rows across every household.
jobs.confirmDisableBody: It stops running until it is enabled again. Nothing catches up the runs it misses while disabled.
jobs.confirmEnableBody: It resumes on its normal cadence from the next tick.
jobs.resultNotClaimed: Nothing ran: another replica holds the lease, or the job was not due. The lease was not taken.
jobs.resultTruncated: The sweep stopped before the table was exhausted and was recorded as FAILED. A partial fan-out is not a success.
jobs.resultRan: Ran: {{executed}} executed, {{skipped}} already done, {{rows}} rows affected.
jobs.resultEnabled: Enabled. It resumes on its normal cadence.
jobs.resultDisabled: Disabled. It will not run until re-enabled.

outbox.title: Outbox & dead letters
outbox.intro: Events that could not be delivered. The outbox has had a DEAD status and a retry limit for a long time; nothing has ever displayed it, and because the backlog gauge counts only pending work, a message dying made that gauge go quieter.
outbox.readingHealthy: Nothing has died. Pending work is being drained normally.
outbox.readingRelayStalled: Dead letters AND a pending backlog: this reads as the relay having stopped rather than one poisoned message.
outbox.readingPoison: Dead letters with no pending backlog: this reads as specific messages that fail every time, not a stalled relay.
outbox.confirmBody: They will be delivered again on the next relay pass. Do this once the thing that was failing is healthy — a message that has failed eight times may fail forever.
outbox.confirmIdempotent: Safe to press twice: recovery only moves rows that are still dead, and redelivery collides on the event and notification unique keys rather than duplicating a reward, an event or a notification.

deliveries.title: Notification backlog
deliveries.intro: How many notifications are queued, how many died permanently, and of which types. Counts and type names only — no title, no body, no household. Triaging «FCM credentials are rotated» does not need to know which family, and an operator console is not a place a child's notification text should be readable.
deliveries.scopeCaveat: THESE NUMBERS COVER THE DEFERRED PATH ONLY — notifications held by quiet hours and released by the sweep. The immediate path computes its push outcome and discards it, so a zero here does NOT mean every notification arrived. It means no deferred notification exhausted its attempts.
deliveries.notMeasured: What this screen cannot tell you
deliveries.gapReason: There is no per-notification operator route on the backend — no retry, no cancel, no inspect by id. Nor could this page join one client-side: the decision log stores no notification id, only a source event id.
deliveries.immediateGapReason: The immediate push path does not persist its outcome, so an FCM failure outside quiet hours is recorded nowhere — not as a row, not as a counter, not as an error string.

aiUsage.title: AI cost
aiUsage.intro: What the model spent, by feature, over a window. Derived from token counts and a rate table in code, which is why every figure here says estimated.
aiUsage.noUsage: No AI call was recorded in this window.
aiUsage.notMeasured: What this screen cannot tell you
aiUsage.gapFamilyReason: No per-household breakdown is offered here. The family id IS recorded on every call made in a household's context — the tenant layer stamps it — and is left empty only for calls made by a platform job, where empty is the honest value. So the breakdown is buildable; this endpoint simply groups by feature and by nothing else.
aiUsage.gapFailureReason: This is what ANSWERED cost. A call that timed out, was refused by the safety layer, tripped the circuit breaker, or fell through to the deterministic template writes no row at all — failures are not a smaller number here, they are absent from the table.
